races.name: Unibet/british Stallion Studs Ebf Fillies' Novice Stakes (gbb Race)
Unibet/Breeders Backing Racing EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: It Would Be You
runners_data.note: A 4yo with a strong form profile (OR 120, win over 16f at Goodwood), 125 days off but Jennie Candlish has a strong 14-day strike rate; sits prominently just off the pace in the ideal position to capitalise on Manaar's uncontested lead, and the step back up in distance is a clear positive given her stamina-biased profile.

runners_data.name: Manaar
runners_data.note: William Haggas filly with a recent 25-day turnaround, form figures of 1-2 suggest reliability; gets to lead unopposed under Cieren Fallon and controls every variable in the race, though she steps up sharply in trip and must prove she stays 1m4f on a surface that is Standard to Slow.

runners_data.name: Arrivera
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's 3yo has a sim-going record of 0 wins and 1 place on Standard, and form of 6-2 shows inconsistency; David Egan is a positive booking, but 69 days off and a hold-up style means she needs the front runners to have gone too hard — not guaranteed with Manaar likely to conserve energy.

runners_data.name: Ladykirk
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's 3yo carries the lowest OR in the field at 74 and her form of 2-5-5 shows a filly that finds placed spots but struggles to win; the hold-up style asks for a strong pace scenario that is unlikely to materialise, and 82 days between runs adds another layer of uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Lunella
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's 3yo showed useful form placing over 10f and 12f at Goodwood; Jack Mitchell is a shrewd booking and her prominent style maps her ideally to track Manaar at close range, making her one of the main dangers to the likely leaders if she has trained on since her last run 28 days ago.

races.paceDynamic: Manaar is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-runner field and, with no rival willing to dispute the lead, Cieren Fallon will be able to dictate an entirely uncontested, measured gallop over this 1m4f trip on a Standard to Slow Kempton surface. It Would Be You and Lunella will track in prominent positions just behind, while Arrivera and Ladykirk are both hold-up types who will be asked to close from the rear on what is likely to be a generous but controlled tempo. Standard to Slow conditions at Kempton over this distance tend to stretch the field and reward those with stamina and tactical positioning rather than a pure turn-of-foot, meaning a lone pacesetter controlling the fractions can dictate matters to the line if fit and well. This race shape strongly favours prominently-raced types who can sit close to Manaar without expending energy, as the hold-up runners will need to generate a sustained run from some way out on ground that will blunt a short, sharp finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Manaar Controls, Tracks Close
scenarios.trigger: If Manaar dictates an uncontested lead and the pace remains sustainable throughout, allowing close-tracking rivals to pounce.
scenarios.body: Manaar sets the fractions exactly as Haggas/Fallon intend, and It Would Be You or Lunella, sitting a length or two off the pace, exploit their prominent positions to collar the leader late or run on past a tiring front-runner; Standard to Slow going rewards stamina and position over raw speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overrun Manaar
scenarios.trigger: If It Would Be You or Lunella press Manaar more aggressively than expected, forcing a contested tempo that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: A more pressured early pace would drain Manaar and leave the prominent challengers themselves vulnerable to a well-timed late sweep; the Standard to Slow surface would amplify the stamina test and potentially help a fresh hold-up horse if the front group ties up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a true closing run for the rear-seated pair.
scenarios.body: Arrivera, with two placed efforts on similar Standard going and David Egan in the saddle, is best equipped of the hold-up runners to produce a sustained finish if the leaders have over-cooked it; Ladykirk's form figures suggest she struggles to convert placed runs into wins and is the less likely beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Manaar crawls and no rival applies pressure, turning it into a flat-speed dash over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Standard to Slow ground at Kempton over 1m4f rarely produces a true sprint finish, making this the least likely outcome; in such a scenario older, higher-rated horses with tactical versatility like It Would Be You would be best suited.

watchPoints.text: Manaar's stamina at 1m4f is unproven — if she struggles to see out the trip, It Would Be You and Lunella are positioned to pounce immediately and the race outcome could swing sharply against the front-runner in the final furlong.

It Would Be You returns after 125 days off; if she is not fully wound up, Lunella — who was out only 28 days ago and ran a solid third last time — could be the sharper of the two prominent-racing challengers.

Arrivera's David Egan booking elevates her hold-up chance, but her 0 wins from 1 placed run on similar going and a 69-day absence mean punters should watch how she travels early — if she is not moving sweetly by halfway, her chance is likely minimal.

Standard to Slow ground is confirmed for all Kempton 1m4f races tonight; any horse that appears to struggle in the going early (particularly the hold-up runners who must generate a sustained run) should be discounted quickly as the race develops.

With only five runners, the field is small enough that Fallon on Manaar could easily control fractions to within a stride — watch whether any prominent rival applies pressure from the two-mile gate, as any early pressure on the leader would fundamentally change the race shape.

races.name: Unibet Support Safer Gambling Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Percy's Lad
runners_data.note: Prominent-style eight-year-old trained by Kubler who has solid course form at this trip and similar going (2 places from 15 runs in Standard); Nader's booking is workmanlike and OR 86 makes him competitive at the top of the weights, though recent form shows 6th and 13th finishes suggesting he needs things to fall right.
runners_data.comment: Percy's Lad showed sharp improvement when second two starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and going to call on; winless in his last five starts remains the caveat, though a rating of 97 marks him as the one to beat from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Dapper Guest
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse for Queally and Margarson who has placed twice in 15 runs on similar going; the visor is noted, he ran four times over today's 7f on Good and placed once, and 19 days since last run is a manageable gap — needs a searching pace to deliver his finish.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Dapper Guest faces a stiff task here; an eighth last time out and an unplaced effort two starts back offer little encouragement, though he has run over today's trip and goes to post fresh enough on 19 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Eminency
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Cieren Fallon wearing a tongue-strap, with a 3rd and a 7th in his last two starts on Standard going over this exact trip; 16 days since last run is fine, and three places from 15 runs on similar going suggests he can hit the frame if the pace suits his style.
runners_data.comment: Eminency arrives in sound nick after 16 days off, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour, and our rating of 90 marks him as a strong contender — though he is winless in his last six starts, and that seventh last time out is the concern.

runners_data.name: Cogitate
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Charles Bishop and Eve Johnson Houghton wearing a visor, with a 4th in Standard over 7f last time and three places from 15 outings on similar going; has done his best work at 8f and this drop back to 7f on an AW surface with give may catch him slightly out.
runners_data.comment: Cogitate shaped with real promise when third three starts back and runner-up six starts back, and having run over today's trip and going he arrives fit on a 16-day turnaround carrying 133 lb from stall nine; the concern is he has been winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Brosay
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for Nicola Currie who has no win or place from two starts on similar going; his recent form is entirely over sprint trips (5f-6f) making this 7f assignment on Standard to Slow a significant concern, and Charlie Pike has drawn a blank in his last six runners.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Brosay does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 16 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; however, his recent finishes — including two unplaced efforts — make it hard to fancy him strongly from stall 8 off 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Orchid
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for the in-form Loughnane and Boughey stable; wears a tongue-strap and holds a 4th on Standard at 7f and multiple placings in similar conditions (4 places from 10 runs), making him one of the better-placed runners to track the pace and challenge in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Orchid arrives here 12 days fresh, has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating edges above her official mark — but a fourth as best recent finish from draw 11 off 131 lb makes a breakthrough tough to call.

runners_data.name: Flag Of St George
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Fraser and Chapple-Hyam, wearing a hood; has placed twice on Standard at this trip and OR 80 is competitive — the key question is whether Arctician's presence forces an unsustainable early duel or whether one of the two can break clear and control the tempo.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Flag Of St George at least has experience over today's trip, but a seventh last time out and eighth two back make encouragement hard to find; stall one and 130 lb add further questions at a competitive level.

runners_data.name: Sea Founder
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up horse at heart who has won at 8f on Standard and placed at 12f, so this 7f on AW with a congested field may force him to race closer than he'd like; Richard Hughes has had two winners from 30 runners in the last 14 days and the horse's best form has come at longer trips.
runners_data.comment: Sea Founder won three starts back and brings both distance and going experience, but his last two runs have yielded a ninth and a sixth, and at 127 lb from stall two he faces a stiff ask to recapture that earlier form.

runners_data.name: Longlai
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up operator for Benoit de la Sayette and George Baker, last seen 54 days ago; his best recent finish on Standard was 4th of 4 over 7f and he has struggled lately (12th, 7th in previous runs on this surface) — the layoff and current form make him one of the harder cases to get enthusiastic about.
runners_data.comment: Longlai brings strong credentials here, with experience of today's trip and conditions and a rating of 90 that suggests he's well ahead of his official mark — though he's winless in his last five starts, and that inconsistency is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Arctician
runners_data.note: Second confirmed front-runner for Harry Davies and Simon Dow, last seen 61 days ago after a relatively busy AW campaign; has placed five times from 15 outings on Standard going at 7f-8f, so the surface holds no fears, and the longer break may have freshened him up — will contest the lead with Flag Of St George from the outset.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with an eighth last time out and a seventh two starts back, Arctician returns after 61 days off rated ninth of the twelve on our figures — experience over today's trip and going offers slim comfort, but he faces a stiff task from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Peter The Wolf
runners_data.note: Wears a hood for Edward Greatrex and Warren Greatrex; has won over 6f on Soft and carries natural hold-up tendencies, though in this race he is likely to be pushed into a more forward position than ideal due to the volume of hold-up types — his best form is at shorter trips and the step to 7f on AW is worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, Peter The Wolf has finished seventh and unplaced in his last two starts, making him hard to fancy despite a win five starts back and experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Nezeeh
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for William Cox and Jim & Suzi Best, 37 days since last run; all five historical runs in the form string have been over 5f-6f, making this 7f assignment a clear distance query, and he has no wins or places from three runs on Standard going — the redistribution into a midfield slot compounds an already difficult ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts with a string of eighth-place finishes and unplaced efforts, Nezeeh is hard to fancy ranked bottom of the field on our figures; he has run over today's trip, and 37 days between runs suggests he returns fresh, but that may count for little given recent struggles.

races.paceDynamic: Flag Of St George and Arctician are the two confirmed front-runners and will fight for the lead from the off, creating a genuinely contested pace over Kempton's 7f on a Standard to Slow surface that will stretch the field early and reward those who can sustain their gallop into the straight. With the going carrying on the slower side, the early exchanges between these two are unlikely to be scorching but will be honest enough to ensure the race is run on merits rather than developing into a sprint finish. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than the map can physically accommodate at the rear — Sea Founder, Longlai, Peter The Wolf and Nezeeh are natural hold-up horses who will be competing for positions they may not truly secure, meaning the midfield is likely to be congested and passage-finding will be critical for those types. This race shape — two front-runners pressing each other on a surface with give — most favours prominent racers tracking just off the pace who can exploit any weakness from the leaders without being caught in the hold-up traffic further back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Flag Of St George and Arctician press each other honestly and fade in the final furlong, allowing prominent trackers to overhaul them.
scenarios.body: The contested front-running pace sets it up perfectly for horses sitting a length or two off the leaders, who can time their run without fighting through traffic; on Standard to Slow going the leaders will find the final furlong testing after their duel.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters — most plausibly Flag Of St George — gains a clear advantage early and the challengers fail to reel them in.
scenarios.body: A clear lead on Standard to Slow going can be a significant asset at Kempton 7f if the front-runner settles after breaking clear; Flag Of St George has placed twice at this course and trip in similar going and could exploit a fractional lead if Arctician cracks early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners burn each other out quickly and a well-positioned midfield runner threads through to take full advantage.
scenarios.body: Congestion in the midfield means only the sharpest movers will find a clear run; Cogitate and Eminency both have placings at this course and trip in Standard, giving them the best credentials among this group to finish off strongly if the pace is truly honest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely or the field fans wide, gifting true closers a clear passage to deliver a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Sea Founder, Longlai and Peter The Wolf are the natural finishers but all three face the challenge of racing out of their preferred role in a field this competitive for rear positions; only a genuinely fast pace that burns up the leaders makes this realistic, and the redistribution of so many hold-up types reduces the probability markedly.

watchPoints.text: Flag Of St George and Arctician will lock horns for the lead immediately — if Arctician refuses to settle behind, both could set a pace that flatters the prominent stalkers but leaves the front two spent entering the final furlong.

Sea Founder, Longlai, Peter The Wolf and Nezeeh are all natural hold-up horses competing for fewer rear positions than exist — watch for congestion and checked runs in the midfield/rear group from the 3f pole, which could cause significant interference.

Orchid (Loughnane/Boughey) is one of the few horses whose natural prominent style fits this race shape perfectly — if he gets a clean passage tracking the pace, he warrants close monitoring turning for home.

Standard to Slow going is confirmed for this race and is subtly slower than pure Standard — horses with proven form in that precise band (Eminency, Cogitate, Flag Of St George) hold a marginal edge over those whose similar-going records are exclusively on Good.

Arctician is 61 days since his last run and Longlai is 54 days — both are among the longer layoffs in the field, and both horses have been consistent enough in the past to suggest fitness is likely, but neither trainer has strong recent form figures to provide confidence.

races.name: Unibet Support Safer Gambling Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Wild Nature
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse who needs things to happen in front of her; won over this C&D trip on Standard and has sound going stats, but with so many closers competing for the same late run, a clear passage is far from guaranteed at a compact Kempton 7f.|
runners_data.comment: Wild Nature arrives here fit on a 33-day break, has run over today's trip and going, and that winning effort — a victory four starts back — plus a third three starts back highlights the ability within him; the worry is consecutive unplaced runs since.

runners_data.name: Philanthropist
runners_data.note: Progressive sort who won over this course and trip on Good and showed guts at Kempton in his last run; the prominent style is perfectly aligned with the race shape here and George Wood's positive approach should see him well positioned throughout.|
runners_data.comment: Philanthropist arrives with a win and a third in recent starts, races off stall one carrying 134 lb, and has experience over today's trip and conditions — a strong profile. The risk is his unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Metal Merchant
runners_data.note: Consistent plodder but his form string of 0-0004 with a best recent finish of fourth tells the story; a hold-up operator who has not finished in the first three on this surface or going in fifteen attempts, making it hard to get excited.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five but Metal Merchant has run over today's trip and going before, and a return to form fourth last time out offers encouragement at a competitive 133 lb; 18 days between runs leaves him nicely fresh.

runners_data.name: Chalk Mountain
runners_data.note: Won twice at Kempton on Standard, including over this course and distance, and the tongue-tie is retained; Alfie Redman's 7lb claim makes the weight look attractive and the prominent style dovetails neatly with the expected race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Ran well last time out when second, though his three starts prior to that were disappointing; has run over today's trip and going, and 16 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, but 132 lb is a notable burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Racingbreaks Ryder
runners_data.note: Landed a course win over a mile on Standard and drops back to 7f here; Jason Watson is positive and the hold-up style with a well-timed run suits a scenario where the front end weakens, though 47 days off is a minor flag.|
runners_data.comment: Racingbreaks Ryder arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's distance and going, while our rating of 89 marks him out as a serious threat from stall 11; the concern is 47 days off the track since that victory.

runners_data.name: Bridget's View
runners_data.note: Consistent in frame finishes at 7-8f but has never won at Kempton and the true hold-up style — pushed into a midfield slot here because the rear is crowded — means she needs a very specific set of circumstances to get involved at the business end.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and beaten into sixth last time out, Bridget's View has experience of today's trip and conditions in her favour, but at 130 lb from stall 5, her recent consistency concerns outweigh her credentials at this level.

runners_data.name: Kiniro
runners_data.note: All six career wins came at 6f and he has never raced beyond that trip until now, which is the defining concern; a genuine hold-up horse placed in midfield by necessity rather than choice, and the step up to 7f on a slow surface is a significant unknown.|
runners_data.comment: Kiniro won five starts back in his recent form but has been inconsistent since, finishing eighth last time out after 46 days off; he has run over today's trip and going, and while a second two starts back offers hope, the layoff and stall eight add mild uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Kitaro Kich
runners_data.note: Boasts strong course form — three wins at Kempton on Standard — and the tongue-tie is in place; a natural closer whose redistribution to midfield is a slight compromise, but the depth of experience over C&D keeps him firmly in calculations if the pace scenario offers even a crack.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Kitaro Kich makes hard work of recommendation after finishing seventh last time out, fourth two starts back, and sixth three starts back; the one bright spot is a win four starts back, and he does have experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Lady Mariko
runners_data.note: Disappointing recent run of 160606 and her three wins have all come at 6f on fast ground; the step to 7f on a slow surface combined with being a true hold-up horse placed out of position makes this a tough assignment.|
runners_data.comment: A winner in her last six starts but that sole victory sits six runs back, and a run of 6ths and unplaced efforts since tells its own story; has experience of today's trip and going, and 125 lb from stall 2 gives her a chance, though recent consistency is the concern.

runners_data.name: How Impressive
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front runner and the key pace ingredient; won at Kempton and can dictate here, but the OR of 74 means he is giving lumps of weight away and his recent form of P42900 suggests he is on the downgrade, raising questions about how long he can hold on.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with consecutive unplaced efforts before that, How Impressive is hard to fancy ranked last on our figures here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 33 days between runs suggests he arrives reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Berry Clever
runners_data.note: Consistent place-getter with five of his last six runs producing a top-five finish; the prominent style suits the anticipated shape and De Sousa's presence adds tactical nous, though he has yet to win on Standard going in seven attempts.|
runners_data.comment: Berry Clever has mustered just one win in his last six starts, finishing fourth three times in that sequence, and our figures rank him ninth of eleven — hard to fancy. He has run over today's distance and going, and a 20-day turnaround suggests he arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: How Impressive is the lone confirmed front runner and, on Standard to Slow Kempton AW, is likely to dictate from gate to line at a controlled, uncontested gallop that could turn this 7f contest into a thorough test of stamina over the final two furlongs. Philanthropist and Chalk Mountain are the natural prominent types who will look to track closely, with Berry Clever also likely to press forward and fill out the pace picture just behind the leader. The Standard to Slow surface will stretch the field early and reward those who travel efficiently in the first half of the race, making it hard for genuine hold-up horses to bridge the gap in the closing stages. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can latch onto How Impressive's shoulder and use the steady early gallop to their advantage, rather than deep closers who will find the front trio already well-organised and the surface too unforgiving for a late sweeping run. Note that the field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Bridget's View, Kiniro, Kitaro Kich and Lady Mariko are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield, and How Impressive and Philanthropist are most likely to secure their natural positions at the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Controls
scenarios.trigger: If How Impressive sets an uncontested pace and a prominent tracker travels smoothly into contention from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: The slow surface ensures How Impressive's fractions are manageable and the horse who sits a length or two off the leader with cover will be best placed to pounce; Philanthropist and Chalk Mountain both have strong form on this surface and distance and are ideally positioned to strike.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closer Lands
scenarios.trigger: If How Impressive sets a faster-than-expected pace under pressure and weakens sharply in the final furlong, opening the door for a hold-up horse.
scenarios.body: The Standard to Slow conditions mean any horse who goes too hard early will pay dearly, and a late surge becomes viable if the front end crumbles inside the final 150 yards; Racingbreaks Ryder and Wild Nature both like to come from off the pace and have the finishing kick to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Race, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is truly dawdling and a midfield mover delivers a well-timed run to hit the line with momentum.
scenarios.body: Kiniro and Kitaro Kich are redistributed hold-up types placed in midfield — if the race genuinely compresses and gaps open, a mid-division push could land; their style fit scores (0.91/0.92) temper confidence, but both carry course-and-distance form that keeps them in the frame.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Rush Swamps Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong throughout and the closers get an unimpeded run down the centre of the track in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Lady Mariko and Bridget's View are both true hold-up horses who need everything to fall right; their redistribution to midfield means they are already out of role and the Standard to Slow surface further reduces the likelihood of a winning late burst from deep.

watchPoints.text: Chalk Mountain's course record (two wins at Kempton on Standard) combined with the tongue-tie and a 7lb claim from Redman makes him a significant danger if he secures a prominent pitch behind How Impressive.
Kiniro has never raced beyond 6f — watch how Billy Loughnane manages him in the first quarter-mile, as any signs of greenness or fading at the 2f pole will confirm the trip is beyond him today.

How Impressive (P42900 recent form) is the race's sole pace-maker but his declining form raises a real risk of stopping sharply; if he drops away before the final furlong the entire pace map collapses and the finish could be chaotic.

Metal Merchant has zero wins or places on this surface in fifteen attempts — if he drifts in-play on Betfair, that market signal is a reliable indicator the field has priced him out correctly and no adjustment is needed.

Berry Clever has never won on Standard going in seven runs despite consistently threatening; watch whether De Sousa slots him closer to the pace than usual, which would be a meaningful jockey-driven change of approach.

races.name: Bet £20 Get £20 With Unibet Handicap Stakes (London Mile Series Qualifier) (Div I)

runners_data.name: Warrior Mode
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by Sir Mark Prescott, whose string is in form (4 wins from 23 runners in the past 14 days); recent third at Goodwood is solid recent evidence and 25 days between runs is ideal freshness, but closing from the rear on a Standard to Slow surface is an ask.
runners_data.comment: Warrior Mode shaped well when third last time out and was third again four starts back, showing he can hit the frame on his day; our rating has him narrowly top-rated here, and with experience over today's trip and going, he carries 143 lb from draw 6 — the worry is he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Foreseen
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, set to dictate on his own terms; has won twice at this course and distance in similar going and Tony Carroll's yard has been busy; 61 days off is a mild question, but the tactical advantage of leading uncontested is significant.
runners_data.comment: Foreseen won two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims on conditions; carrying 141 lb from stall nine, the 61-day absence is the one query, but his overall profile makes him our pick here.

runners_data.name: Stardancer
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance at Goodwood last time but that was on Good ground, and the switch to Standard to Slow on the all-weather is a notable shift for a horse who has only placed twice in seven runs on similar going; Georgia Dobie takes off a useful 3lb claim.
runners_data.comment: Stardancer won last time out but that victory came 46 days ago, leaving a fitness question, and he has been out of the frame in two of his four most recent starts. Has run over today's trip and carries 139 lb from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Grey Soul
runners_data.note: Consistent and in fine recent form with three wins from nine similar-going starts; Jason Watson is an experienced Kempton pilot and the horse's prominent racing style is perfectly tailored to this slow-tempo shape — one of the most naturally positioned horses in the race.
runners_data.comment: Grey Soul arrives on the back of two consecutive wins and has run over today's trip and going, but he hasn't raced in 44 days and carries 139 lb, which could blunt his recent momentum.

runners_data.name: Metallo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has placed four times in 15 starts on similar going without winning; recent form shows a string of fourth-place finishes and David Egan cannot disguise the lack of a finishing kick, with the Standard to Slow surface unlikely to help his cause.
runners_data.comment: Metallo has run over today's trip and going before and, rated 85 by us against an official mark of 75, looks significantly ahead of his handicap assessment — the chief concern is a winless recent run of six starts, with an unplaced effort last time out 44 days ago leaving fitness to prove.

runners_data.name: Kindest Nation
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up specialist who has been mapped into midfield due to the surplus of rear-division types; has varied going preference (hg:v) which may be pertinent, and a 61-day absence plus a string of disappointing recent runs (including a 10th and a 9th) make this a difficult proposition even if he does secure his natural position.
runners_data.comment: Kindest Nation showed she can win in her last five starts, with that victory coming five starts back, and she has experience over today's trip and going — the concern is a return from 61 days off and recent unplaced efforts casting doubt on current form.

runners_data.name: I Am Me
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with genuine Kempton course form — has placed three times at this track over the mile in similar going — and Cieren Fallon's experience at the track is an asset; 63 days off is worth noting, but his style is well-suited to sitting just off the pace in a steady-run race.
runners_data.comment: Boasts a win two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, but that ninth last time out — after 63 days off — is the clear concern; 133 lb from stall 1 adds a further test for a horse needing to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Beauty By My Side
runners_data.note: Out-of-form gelding whose true hold-up style has been displaced into midfield given the crowded rear; five consecutive poor runs including two 10ths and a 15th make it hard to identify a route back to competitiveness, and the Standard to Slow surface does nothing to help a horse who needs a strong pace to close into.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Beauty By My Side faces a stiff task ranked eighth on our figures, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a reasonable 32-day break carrying 131 lb from stall five.

runners_data.name: Lili Marleen
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish — a particularly damaging trait on a track and in conditions that reward those who conserve energy; has raced just 12 days ago and has a concerning recent form string including falls/pulled-up, and her natural hold-up style being pushed into midfield only compounds the risks.
runners_data.comment: Lili Marleen's recent starts make grim reading — a fall, a pull-up and a ninth among her last four outings — and our figures rank her last of ten. She has run over today's trip, and a win five starts back is the slender comfort here.

runners_data.name: Cotswold Cottage
runners_data.note: Six-year-old returning from a significant 320-day absence, and all five of her recent runs have been at 9f-12f on Soft or Standard ground — coming back in trip to a mile on the all-weather after nearly a year off makes her profile very hard to assess; true hold-up style is squeezed into midfield by the field's composition.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy 320-day absence is the dominant concern here, and our figures rank her ninth of ten in this field. She has run over today's trip and does own two wins in her last five starts — including a recent victory — but freshness at this level is a significant ask.

races.paceDynamic: Foreseen is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner mile handicap and, with no significant challenger pressing from the gates, is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on what is riding Standard to Slow — conditions that tend to compress the field and make it harder for genuine hold-up horses to generate the momentum they need late on. Grey Soul will look to sit prominently just off the pace, and I Am Me is another who prefers to race close to the action, so Foreseen will have company but is unlikely to be seriously pressured into going too fast. The Standard to Slow surface rewards economy of effort, which strongly favours the horse or horses able to track the pace without cover and pounce in the straight rather than those required to close from a genuine position of disadvantage. This shape overwhelmingly suits prominent racers and pace-stalkers who travel within striking range, while the substantial cluster of true hold-up horses — Kindest Nation, Beauty By My Side, Lili Marleen, and Cotswold Cottage — have all been redistributed on the map because there are more back-of-the-field types in this field than can realistically find their natural position; Grey Soul and I Am Me are best placed to secure a genuine prominent berth behind Foreseen.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Foreseen Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Foreseen sets a measured, uncontested pace and the stalking duo of Grey Soul and I Am Me track within two lengths throughout.
scenarios.body: Foreseen's controlled fractions on the Standard to Slow surface create a race run at a tempo that suits those racing prominently, and Grey Soul or I Am Me — both genuine prominent types with the course form to match — are ideally positioned to pounce inside the final furlong; the hold-up contingent simply cannot generate sufficient late momentum from a standing start on this surface.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Foreseen Bowls Them Over
scenarios.trigger: If the Standard to Slow conditions slow the overall tempo enough that Foreseen's controlled front-running becomes an unassailable advantage and no one can close.
scenarios.body: Foreseen has won twice on Standard Kempton ground and if the pace is truly dawdling the field may never get close enough to challenge; a slow-run mile on this surface can leave the leader with an insurmountable advantage if the kick-back never comes.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly stronger than expected and opens a gap for a horse like Warrior Mode or Stardancer to finish strongly from mid-division.
scenarios.body: A fractionally stronger early tempo — perhaps sparked by Grey Soul pressing Foreseen — would use up the leaders and create the gap a genuine staying-type closer needs; Warrior Mode's recent course-amenable form and Stardancer's ability to finish off a race make them the most credible threats from this group.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Overcrowded Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of multiple hold-up types into the middle of the field causes traffic problems that scramble the race shape entirely and a wide outsider benefits.
scenarios.body: With Kindest Nation, Beauty By My Side, Lili Marleen, and Cotswold Cottage all racing out of their natural roles and bunched in mid-division, a wall of horses in the straight is a genuine risk; any runner caught in traffic could be beaten while a horse who threads a gap — most plausibly Warrior Mode with Dylan Hogan's steering — could emerge late.

watchPoints.text: Foreseen holds a decisive positional advantage as the lone front-runner — watch whether Grey Soul or I Am Me press him, because if they do not, he may simply coast to victory on his own terms.

The cluster of displaced hold-up types (Kindest Nation, Beauty By My Side, Lili Marleen, Cotswold Cottage) all competing for midfield real estate creates a genuine traffic risk in the straight — watch for trouble in running around the two-furlong pole.

The Standard to Slow surface is slower than the listed going of Standard — any horse who needs a true end-to-end gallop to finish off the race (Metallo, Lili Marleen) is at a structural disadvantage and should be monitored for early signs of struggling to land a blow.

Cotswold Cottage returns from 320 days off with all recent form at longer trips on different surfaces — watch her market moves closely in the morning; any support would suggest a schooling run on the way to a bigger target, while drifting would confirm cold stats.

Stardancer's win came at Goodwood on Good ground, making this Standard to Slow all-weather surface a significant change of conditions — watch early in the race to see whether she travels with her usual fluency or already looks uncomfortable.

races.name: Bet £20 Get £20 With Unibet Handicap Stakes (London Mile Series Qualifier) (Div II)

runners_data.name: Final Night
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for John Butler who shaped well last time at Goodwood (3rd, 2nd in five recent starts at 8f on Good); the soft side of Standard To Slow is fine for her and Billy Loughnane will aim to dictate — the key risk is whether the modest pace she sets flatters rivals.
runners_data.comment: Final Night arrives here in good nick after finishing second last time out, and with experience of today's trip and going, he rates a strong each-way threat off a mark of 80 — though winless in his last six starts, consistency remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Gallant
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the ride on this hold-up handler who has struggled for form over shorter distances on Good ground; the step to 1m on this surface is a query, form figures read 607573 and the 19-day break is unexceptional — needs much more pace than this race is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Gallant shaped with plenty of promise when third last time out, and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour; the worry is that he has been winless in his last six starts, and his consistency will need to sharpen up here.

runners_data.name: Rogue Allegiance
runners_data.note: Excellent recent form (221 in last three) for James Owen, racing prominently enough to capitalise on a stolen lead; Harry Davies has experience placing him well and the 7f Goodwood form translates comfortably to a Kempton mile — looks the most dangerous rival to the leader.
runners_data.comment: Rogue Allegiance arrives in decent nick after a win last time out, and has run over today's trip and going, but his run of placed efforts before that victory suggest he can be edged out at the business end, and 139 lb is no lightweight burden.

runners_data.name: City Of Kings
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' six-year-old is a genuine deep-closer at heart, though the map shows him in midfield because the race has too many natural hold-up horses to accommodate them all; his flat recent form (516/00) on similar surfaces is hard to overcome regardless of positioning.
runners_data.comment: Three consecutive unplaced efforts make City Of Kings hard to fancy, and he ranks ninth of ten on our figures; he has run over today's trip before and returns on a reasonable 16-day turnaround, but little else stands out.

runners_data.name: Sovereign View
runners_data.note: James Tate's lightly-raced three-year-old has strong Standard-going course form (won and placed on this surface, 7/9 sim-going strike-rate) and Jason Watson knows the track well; the prominent headgear (p) could sharpen him up and a handicap mark of 82 makes him competitive if he reproduces his best.
runners_data.comment: Sovereign View shaped with promise when third one start back and has experience of today's trip and conditions; our rating of 96 heads the field, and at 137 lb from stall seven he remains the one to beat, albeit a return to winning form is needed.

runners_data.name: San Juanito
runners_data.note: A confirmed deep hold-up type at heart, shifted toward midfield on the map only because of the volume of closers in this field; 44-day break, a poor recent record (007-90) and a stat of 13th and 9th on Standard surface last two outings make him very difficult to fancy in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, San Juanito nevertheless carries an 83 rating into this, suggesting more ability than his official mark of 74 implies, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the concern is a string of unplaced efforts that will need reversing.

runners_data.name: Dumuji
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's three-year-old is the only other prominent-style runner and PJ McDonald is an ideal pilot for a horse who wants to track the leader; three 5th-placed finishes on Good after his debut win on Standard AW suggest he needs this surface, making the track a positive switch.
runners_data.comment: Dumuji won one start back from an unplaced effort last time, and he has run over today's trip and going before; however, ranked sixth of ten on our rating and carrying 132 lb, he faces a stiff ask to reverse that recent dip in form.

runners_data.name: Gunfighter
runners_data.note: David Egan partners this John Butler five-year-old who won on Standard AW 12 days ago over 7f — the natural hold-up style means he is placed further forward on the map than he will likely race; the 1m trip is slightly further than his comfort zone and back-to-back runs can suit some.
runners_data.comment: Gunfighter won one start back but has been disappointing either side of that success, finishing seventh last time out; he has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 79 suggests ability, though consistency remains the concern at 131 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Man Of Desert
runners_data.note: Chris Dwyer's veteran stays 8f well and has placed form at this course; Silvestre De Sousa is a powerful positional jockey who could manufacture a clean run, but the horse's true running style is from the rear and this race shape gives him little to aim at — 41-day break adds further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Man Of Desert faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's trip and going, and the recent second is a crumb of comfort, but 41 days off and 129 lb from stall eight make him difficult to fancy.

runners_data.name: Lieutenant Kije
runners_data.note: The 287-day absence for Tom Ward's three-year-old is the defining angle here — fitness is a genuine and significant concern; placed twice in his short career at 6-7f on Standard, and Kaiya Fraser taking the ride suggests a quiet confidence, but the layoff makes him almost impossible to assess with confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and absent for 287 days, Lieutenant Kije faces a stiff task from stall 10, though he has run over today's trip and going before and did finish second one start back.

races.paceDynamic: Final Night is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no meaningful challenger for the lead, is set to control from the outset at a tempo of her own choosing on a Standard To Slow Kempton surface — conditions that reward those who can sustain rather than sprint. Dumuji is the only other prominent-styled runner and will likely track just off Final Night's shoulder, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly searching. This setup creates a race where the front two dictate proceedings around the sweeping Kempton mile, leaving hold-up horses with a deficit to close that a steady gallop may not fully expose. The tactical verdict is clear: horses racing prominently or tracking the modest pace are best placed, while genuine closers face a stern challenge making up ground without a strong early tempo to exploit. Note that the field is stacked with true hold-up types — City Of Kings, San Juanito, Gunfighter, Man Of Desert and Lieutenant Kije are all natural rear-runners who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there is simply no room for them all to occupy their genuine position; of these, only those blessed with the best sectional speed or a wide draw are likely to land anywhere near the front half.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Final Night Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Final Night bowls along uncontested and sets a modest, energy-conserving pace that suits those tracking close.
scenarios.body: Final Night dictates a controlled tempo that takes the sting out of the closers, with Dumuji the natural beneficiary tracking in second and having the most to gain from a late kick off a sound pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just lively enough to tire Final Night in the final furlong, allowing a close-tracking horse to collar her.
scenarios.body: Sovereign View, who has strong course form on the all-weather and races prominently, is positioned to swoop past a tiring leader; Rogue Allegiance, in excellent recent form and capable of racing handily, could also benefit from a slight end-to-end collapse.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Get Lucky Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and the Standard To Slow conditions drain Final Night's stamina, opening a late window for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Gallant or Rogue Allegiance would need a notably stronger gallop than this race shape projects to reach the principals; even then, redistributed hold-up types such as City Of Kings would need to race far closer than their natural style permits to make the frame.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Chaos Decides
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed field creates traffic problems in the straight, scrambling positions and rewarding the horse with the cleanest run.
scenarios.body: A muddled finish could see a midfield type like Man Of Desert, who stays the mile well and has Silvestre De Sousa's big-race positional instincts, grab an unexpected place; Lieutenant Kije is the wildcard returning from 287 days off and is completely unknown quantity on fitness.

watchPoints.text: Final Night (Billy Loughnane) — watch whether she is allowed to go out and dictate unchallenged or if Dumuji crowds her early; if the pace is completely unchallenged she could prove very hard to reel in.

Sovereign View — watch the draw and whether Jason Watson elects to sit just off the pace rather than deep in the field; if he can track the front pair he is the most dangerous threat given his strong course record.

Rogue Allegiance (Harry Davies) — form reads well (221) but watch whether the field clusters around him at the start, forcing him wider than ideal; his natural style is front-to-prominent and any traffic disruption diminishes his chance.

Lieutenant Kije — 287 days off the track means the paddock inspection is essential; any sign of physical tension, sweating or a round belly should temper expectations drastically before committing to this runner.

Standard To Slow going confirmed for the 8:00 race — this slightly tacky surface will suit horses with AW course form and may blunt the late kick of the genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed toward midfield on the map.

races.name: Unibet More Extra Place Races Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Cumulonimbus
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 410 days off — that layoff is a significant concern on its own, and his last five runs on fast or good ground show only modest form; sim-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from 3 relevant efforts does little to encourage confidence here on Standard to Slow.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and absent for 410 days, Cumulonimbus nonetheless rates the pick of this field on our figures, with distance and going experience in hand; the concern is that layoff and a recent string of poor finishes make him a harder sell on trust.

runners_data.name: The Green Mile
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with a win and a third from two Kempton AW starts at similar trips; Charles Bishop takes the ride for Neil Mulholland and the 1m4f distance looks a proper test of his stamina given he has been competitive over shorter distances this term.
runners_data.comment: Twice a winner in his last five starts, with a third sandwiched in between, The Green Mile brings solid recent form and going experience to the table; 44 days off and 141 lb on his back are the checks against him finding a repeat.

runners_data.name: Bulletin
runners_data.note: Placed in six of his last twelve starts and has course-and-distance experience over 12f on the AW; Jonathan Portman stable is in decent form (T14: 1/12) and Harry Davies takes the ride, but Bulletin's tendency to find one or two too good suggests he needs a genuine test of stamina to win rather than a steadily-run affair.
runners_data.comment: Bulletin has been knocking on the door, third two starts back and a second four starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going gives him every chance off 141 lb; the risk is he's yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Galaxy Star
runners_data.note: Won over 11f at Kempton AW on his most relevant run and has been placed over 16f on soft, suggesting he is versatile; Alan King's yard is placing him here after a 73-day break which brings freshness, and 5lb claimer Harry Vigors reduces the weight burden, though the claim comes at the cost of experience in a tight prominent contest.
runners_data.comment: Galaxy Star won three starts back but has been beaten into fourth and sixth since, and 73 days off the track adds a fitness query; she has run over today's trip and going, and carries 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Forever Penywern
runners_data.note: The race's one confirmed front-runner, trained by Warren Greatrex, who scored at Kempton over 11f and placed over longer trips; with form figures of 3211-1, she arrives in excellent nick and Edward Greatrex knows exactly how to let her stride, making her the pivotal horse around which the entire tactical shape of this race revolves.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last five starts — including back-to-back victories — make Forever Penywern a solid contender, and he has run over today's trip before; however, 38 days off and a stiff 140 lb test him against stronger company ranked seventh of twelve.

runners_data.name: Son Of Man
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner who won over 12f here at Kempton on Standard ground and has placed twice at this venue; David Egan's booking is eye-catching but a 77-day break and his form figure of 0 at this track last time suggest he may need to find improvement — competing for prominent spots in a congested five-way battle complicates his race.
runners_data.comment: Son Of Man shaped well when third and second in consecutive starts before that recent unplaced run, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; back after 77 days, his profile warrants respect off a mark of 84.

runners_data.name: Classical Allusion
runners_data.note: Won over 12f at Kempton on Standard and placed over the same trip; 95-day absence is a minor concern, and Andrew Balding's runner faces a stern test of prominent-position securing given the volume of horses wanting that ground — Callum Hutchinson will need to be sharp from the gate.

runners_data.name: Kokbastau
runners_data.note: Won over 12f at Kempton on Standard going — directly relevant form — and Roger Varian's three-year-old is on a competitive mark of OR 88; Cieren Fallon is a strong booking and the 16-day turnaround suggests the yard is confident; the additional 2f from his last start is the only query in an otherwise strong profile.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, Kokbastau makes little appeal at the weights carrying 132 lb, and a sixth three starts back undermines confidence; in his favour, he arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Duc De Kent
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a patchy recent record including a 16th-place finish over 18f on good and a 9th on Standard going at 11f; Stevie Donohoe rides for Ian Williams, who has a live T14 strike rate (4/43), but this gelding's sim-going record of 0 wins and 2 places from 15 relevant runs signals limited ceiling.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Duc De Kent at least has experience of today's distance and going, and 18 days since his last outing suggests he arrives fresh; carrying 131 lb with a rating of 88 leaves him with plenty to find against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Must Believe
runners_data.note: Has won and placed on AW Standard ground in good recent form (2-4518), and the George Baker yard connection with Cumulonimbus adds interest; by inclination a prominent racer, the sheer volume of horses wanting that early position means he is likely to find himself further back than ideal, which tempers his chance somewhat in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Must Believe returns after 68 days off the track and, ranked ninth of 12 on our figures, faces a stiff ask — that eighth last time out is hard to ignore. He has run over today's trip and going, and a win two starts back offers a shred of hope.

runners_data.name: Dust Cover
runners_data.note: Three career wins including one at 11f on Standard AW, and placed at 16f on the same surface, suggesting the 1m4f trip is viable; a natural front-to-prominent type, the crowded market for those berths makes it probable he ends up racing in a more restrained position than he would choose, which limits how freely he can express his best form.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Dust Cover is hard to fancy despite two wins in his last six starts — a second three starts back is his best recent effort, and consecutive fourth and fifth suggest form is going the wrong way.

runners_data.name: Mathematician
runners_data.note: Won and placed repeatedly on AW Standard surfaces, with a win at 11f here and placed at 10f, so he handles this track and going well; carries headgear and tends to race handy, but with five horses genuinely competing for the prominent slots, he is almost certain to be shuffled wider and further back than his running style demands, making his task harder than a bare reading of his form suggests.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and hard to oppose with confidence, though Mathematician does bring winning form — a winner two starts back and again four starts back — and has experience of today's going.

races.paceDynamic: Forever Penywern is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to pressure her, she is expected to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m4f trip on Standard to Slow Polytrack. Galaxy Star, Bulletin, Son Of Man, Kokbastau, and Classical Allusion all want prominent positions, creating a congested early battle for the berths immediately behind the leader through the first bend and into the back straight. This prominent traffic jam creates real danger two to three furlongs out when the field compresses and routes become blocked, particularly for those drawn wide or slow away. The race shape — a moderate, uncontested pace set by one horse — strongly favours hold-up horses with a sustained late run, as the moderate tempo will compress bunching mid-race and leave a wall in front of closers; however, the single front-runner dictating also means a well-positioned prominent horse sitting second or third can pounce before the hold-up types unwind. Must Believe, Dust Cover, and Mathematician are genuine prominent-types who are unlikely to secure those positions given the volume of competition for them, making their effective role closer to midfield; of the true prominent horses, Kokbastau and Galaxy Star, with their course-form and jockey quality, are best placed to actually win those spots.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Forever Penywern Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Forever Penywern leads without serious pressure and sets a tempo that suits her stamina, allowing her to quicken off a steady pace.
scenarios.body: Forever Penywern has won twice on this course at this trip under similar conditions and with Edward Greatrex in the saddle she is tactically well-placed to dictate; a moderate gallop with no rival willing to commit against her means she never burns reserves and can extend into the straight with energy remaining.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse positioned second or third in the prominent group tracks Forever Penywern throughout and produces a telling challenge entering the straight.
scenarios.body: The congested early battle for the prominent slots is resolved by two or three settling just off the leader, conserving energy while still tracking the pace; Kokbastau, with Kempton form and Cieren Fallon's positional instincts, or Galaxy Star are the likeliest beneficiaries as they can move into contention before hold-up runners have unwound.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace collapses significantly in the final half-mile and creates a sprint finish that allows closers to arrive late with momentum.
scenarios.body: The Green Mile has shown course form at this venue and trips slightly short of today's distance, suggesting the extra furlong of 1m4f suits; Cumulonimbus is the experienced hold-up type but has not run for 410 days, making The Green Mile the more reliable finisher in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Fractures, Chaos Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes interference or a false injection of pace two to three furlongs out, breaking the field into fragments.
scenarios.body: A fractured mid-race shape benefits horses with the ability to quicken sharply from mid-division when gaps open unexpectedly; Mathematician and Dust Cover, though pushed out of their preferred prominent position, carry sufficient Kempton AW form to capitalise if disruption gifts them a clear run.

watchPoints.text: Forever Penywern — if she gains a completely uncontested lead through the first three furlongs, she sets the race on her own terms and every other horse is racing to her timetable; watch how quickly the prominent five settle behind her at the start.

Kokbastau and Galaxy Star — these two are most likely to actually secure prominent positions behind the leader, and a mid-race move by either two to three furlongs out could end the race as a contest before the hold-up horses have room to unwind.

Prominent congestion at the opening bend — with Son Of Man, Bulletin, Classical Allusion, Kokbastau, and Galaxy Star all wanting to be up with the pace, the first bend at Kempton creates a genuine traffic flashpoint; any checked horse here loses rhythm at a critical stage.

The Green Mile — his hold-up style will require a clear run from two furlongs out; if the prominent group causes a wall of horses as the field straightens, he may find his challenge stifled despite finishing strongly.

Must Believe, Dust Cover, Mathematician — all three are at risk of racing out of their natural role; if any of them manages to find a prominent spot due to a slow start from a natural prominent rival, their effective form profile improves materially and they become more dangerous than their mapped position suggests.

races.name: Try Unibet's New Improved Acca Boosts Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Solanna
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old prominent racer in excellent recent form (three wins and a second in last six starts), handles Standard well (sim-going 1W5P), suited by 11f+, and Billy Loughnane's booking for a yard running at 5/18 in the past fortnight makes this a strong candidate in a race that should play to her stalking style.
runners_data.comment: Solanna arrives on the back of a win last time out, and a second two starts back underlines his consistency — he has distance and going experience to call on, and our rating of 76 marks him as a leading rival. The fitness query after 50 days is the one thing to watch.

runners_data.name: Maestro Del Mar
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has disappointed over longer trips lately (10th at 15f, 10th over 10f on Good), and Silvestre De Sousa takes the ride for a yard without a recent winner (T14: 0/7); the trip is theoretically fine but current form and a yard out of form are negatives.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and our figures rank him tenth of eleven here, with a 54-day absence adding further doubt; the one genuine positive is a third last time out, suggesting he retains some ability.

runners_data.name: Naasma
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type whose recent history is all at 13-16f and who has placed twice on Standard going at this sort of trip; Pat Phelan's yard is cold (T14: 0/2) and sim-going record is modest (0W2P), but Kaiya Fraser's claim helps and the longer stamina-based scenario is the one to keep her in.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Naasma nevertheless boasts a third two runs back and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating of 76 marks her as a leading threat — the risk is she finds a way to finish just outside the frame again.

runners_data.name: Roland Garros
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who set up a 1/12f win on Standard most recently, returning quickly (7 days) fitted again with tongue-piece; Alexandra Egan's 7lb claim is a notable aid on a straightforward track, though the sim-going record (2/15, 0W1P) suggests this surface has not historically been kind to this horse.
runners_data.comment: Roland Garros ran well enough to place third last time out, but that seventh two starts back is a concern; he has run over today's trip and carries 140 lb on a quick turnaround of just seven days, leaving his participation here a mix of promise and questions.

runners_data.name: Star Time
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win and three places from six runs on Standard (6/9 sim-going), and Alan King's yard has a recent winner (T14: 1/9); 70 days off is the concern, but 2/12f on Standard last time out is encouraging and Harry Vigors's claim boosts the weight advantage.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last four starts, and 70 days off the track is a fitness query, but Star Time has distance and going experience to call on and a rating that suggests he holds his own here — the second three starts back shows he can get competitive.

runners_data.name: Crooked Path
runners_data.note: Front-runner with decent staying form (1/16f Good, places at 16-17f on Heavy and Soft) returning after 114 days off for a yard firing at 8/51 in the last fortnight — the in-form trainer angle is significant; however, the extended layoff and uncertain fitness are real risks, and this horse has never run on Standard going.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and 114 days absent, Crooked Path arrives with experience over today's trip and a rating of 77 that marks him out as the one to beat — the risk is his recent string of unplaced efforts suggesting he'll need to rediscover his best.

runners_data.name: Imperial Decision
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type — though placed into the midfield map because of the congested rear — who has placed on Standard at shorter distances (sim-going 0W3P); the tongue-piece is new-ish, the yard is cold (T14: 0/3), and 131 days off is a major concern; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.91) suggests it will be hard for this horse to operate as naturally as it would like.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, Imperial Decision at least showed consistency with a third and a second in that sequence, though the unplaced effort latest and a 131-day absence are obvious concerns; he has run over today's trip and going, and 136 lb is no featherweight.

runners_data.name: Eljowhary
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent racer dropping significantly in class and trip scope (all runs at 7f-10f so far), making a step up to 1m4f that is entirely unexplored territory; Eve Johnson Houghton's yard is warm (T14: 7/44), Charles Bishop rides, but the distance question is a serious unknown for a lightly-raced youngster.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked towards the foot of our assessments, Eljowhary faces a stiff ask here; however, he has been freshened by a 45-day break and, carrying 132 lb, could find more at this level if the layoff has sharpened him.

runners_data.name: Semper Femina
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type with a decent place strike rate (2nd at 12f, 2nd at 10f) but no win; Richard Hannon's operation is active (T14: 8/56), Seamus Cronin's claim helps on the weight, and 21 days since last run means fitness is fine — she wants cut in the ground historically though (sim-going: 1/6) which is a concern on Standard to Slow tonight.

runners_data.name: Backer Bilk
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer — mapped to midfield due to the volume of closers in this field, which tempers confidence in a clean run — who has placed at 16f Good and 16f Good recently; headgear of a hood (hg:h) is noted, the yard is quiet (T14: 1/4), and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) signals this horse may struggle to replicate natural tactics given the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a distant eighth last time out and an official mark of 56, Backer Bilk is hard to fancy against stronger rivals here; he has run over today's trip and going before, but his speed rating of 53 leaves plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Maywedance
runners_data.note: True hold-up type redistributed to midfield because the rear is overcrowded, carrying a STYLE_FIT flag (0.90); best recent profile of the three redistributed closers — two wins at 12f on Standard and form of 407133 — headgear of a hood (hg:p) adds a tightening-up angle, and Jack Mitchell's booking is positive, but the tactical compromise of not finding true hold-up ground is a real obstacle to winning.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and carrying 128 lb, Maywedance is hard to fancy despite consecutive thirds last time out and two starts back; she has experience over today's distance and going, and that lone recent win does at least show she can find the front.

races.paceDynamic: Roland Garros and Crooked Path are the two confirmed front-runners, and with both likely to press for the lead from the off, this race will be run at an honest, contested gallop over 1m4f on a Standard to Slow surface — conditions that will test stamina and punish those who burn too much early fuel. Roland Garros, fitted with a tongue-piece, shapes as the likelier leader given recent course form, but Crooked Path's handler James Owen has been firing (T14: 8/51) and Cieren Fallon aboard will not concede the front without a fight. The resulting genuine pace sets this race up ideally for patient, well-positioned prominent horses who can travel through the race and finish strongly — Solanna and Star Time profile well as beneficiaries, sitting just behind the contested lead without expending unnecessary energy. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can place at the rear — Maywedance, Imperial Decision, and Backer Bilk are all genuine closers but are redistributed into the midfield picture because the strong pace contingent will compress the field; of those three, Maywedance has the best recent course and distance profile and is most likely to secure a workable position despite the congestion.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Suits Patient Prominents
scenarios.trigger: If Roland Garros and Crooked Path fight for the lead and set a genuine honest gallop, leaving the prominent stalkers ideally placed.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off over the final half mile, and horses who have settled just behind the pace in the second rank arrive with the momentum and petrol reserves to take over late; the Standard to Slow surface rewards those with stamina over raw speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Escapes and Holds
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner — most likely Roland Garros — manages to dictate solo without being seriously pressured, controlling the tempo at a comfortable enough clip to conserve energy.
scenarios.body: A manufactured gallop that suits the lead horse allows Roland Garros to steal margins and use the flat Kempton track to sustain its effort; the prominent horses behind lack the acceleration needed to close a comfortable gap late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Carve Through Tiring Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a genuinely strong pace that brings them both back to the field, leaving the late-closers with a wall of tiring horses to pick off.
scenarios.body: A fast early tempo leaves Roland Garros and Crooked Path exhausted entering the straight, and a horse swooping from further back benefits from the carnage; Maywedance, with two wins at 12f on Standard and strong recent form, is best placed to capitalise, though redistribution from natural hold-up ground means this scenario is harder to execute than it appears.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Modest Gallop Muddled Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners neutralise each other early — or one cedes and a crawl develops — the race devolves into a tactical affair with a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A slow-run race removes the stamina edge and turns this into a test of raw speed, favouring a horse who has hidden gate-to-wire ability or a devastating finish from midfield; Eljowhary, dropping in class at three years old, and Semper Femina, who has placed at a good strike rate, could both emerge in a scenario where class and speed trump stamina.

watchPoints.text: Roland Garros and Crooked Path — watch the first two furlongs closely; if both fight hard for the lead, the resulting strong pace could see both fade in the straight and blow the race open for the prominent stalkers.

Crooked Path — returning after 114 days off with no previous run on Standard going; fitness is genuinely uncertain and if this horse struggles to maintain its front-running style, it could cause interference as it drops back through the pack.

Maywedance, Imperial Decision, Backer Bilk — three true hold-up horses redistributed into the midfield picture; watch for a congested midfield early on where these three may struggle to find clear running or their natural position, with potential for scrimmaging between furlongs 1-3.

Eljowhary — has never raced beyond 10f and steps up to 1m4f tonight; watch how Charles Bishop positions this three-year-old early, as an inexperienced stayer in a contested-pace race risks getting outpaced or running out of stamina in the straight.

Star Time — 70 days off for Alan King's yard; watch the market moves and whether this horse travels smoothly in behind the pace, as a well-handicapped prominent racer returning fresh on a going it handles (6/9 sim) could be underestimated.
